The hang wasn't language-specific — `ga` just happened to be where the Copilot CLI wedged. `AiTranslationAdapter.runClaude` called `spawnPrompt` with no timeout, so a child that never exits blocked the chunk (and, at concurrency 4, quickly the whole run) forever with no output.

Changes:
- [docs/scripts/api-translation.ts](docs/scripts/api-translation.ts) — pass `timeoutMs` (env `DOCS_TRANSLATION_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 120000) to `spawnPrompt`. `translateBatch` already logs and skips a failed chunk, so a timed-out batch is left uncached and retried next run instead of stalling.
- [tools/translation-adapters/copilot-wrapper.sh](tools/translation-adapters/copilot-wrapper.sh) and [tools/translation-adapters/agy-wrapper.sh](tools/translation-adapters/agy-wrapper.sh) — run the CLI with `</dev/null` so it can't block on an interactive prompt.
- Documented the knob in [docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md](docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md) plus a changeset.

Tests pass (141). Re-run your command; if a call wedges you'll now see `! skipped a batch of N strings: AI command timed out…` and the run continues.

I also verified the CLI itself: a single call through the wrapper returns in ~6s and its stdout is clean (the `AI Credits / Tokens / Resume` footer goes to stderr, so translations aren't contaminated). If it recurs, lower `DOCS_TRANSLATION_CONCURRENCY` to 1–2 and check `AI Credits` — quota exhaustion is the likeliest trigger given misses begin right at button.md.

content.text:
Those aren't failures — "Interfaces", "Variables", and "Classes" are genuine cognates in French and Catalan, but the passthrough guard treated any source-identical result as a sign of a silently-broken adapter, so it refused to cache them. They were re-sent (and re-paid for) on every run, and never counted toward coverage.

Fix in [docs/scripts/translation-memory.ts](docs/scripts/translation-memory.ts):

- A source-identical value is now cached when **other units in the same batch did change** — that proves the adapter actually worked, so the identical one is a cognate, not an echo. A batch that comes back wholly unchanged still warns and stays a miss.
- The glossary adapter is excluded from that relaxation (`translatesProse === false`); it changes known terms and passes the rest through by design, so its passthroughs must remain misses for a later AI run.
- Deliberate passthroughs are marked so they survive the *read* side of the guard too: a `pantoken-verbatim` flag on the PO entry (`#, pantoken-verbatim`), or a companion marker key in the JSON backend. `diffAgainstCache` serves those cached hits instead of retranslating.

Also added two tests (cognate cached alongside real translations; flagged cache hit served without a CLI call), a changeset, and a note in [docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md](docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md). `vp check` and all 186 docs tests pass.

On your next run those three labels get translated once more, come back identical, and are then cached and flagged — the warnings stop after that.
